q: 1. In which year did Fathimath Dhiyana Saeed resign from her post of Secretary-General?
explain: She resigned in March 2012 before completing her term due to domestic political alignments. The other options represent other years.

q: 2. Who succeeded Fathimath Dhiyana Saeed as Secretary-General on March 12, 2012?
explain: Ahmed Saleem (Maldives) succeeded her to serve the remaining term. The other options are other Secretaries-General.

q: 3. Who is the current Secretary-General of SAARC, assuming office on March 4, 2023?
explain: Golam Sarwar assumed office on March 4, 2023, as the 15th Secretary-General. The other options represent past Secretaries-General.

q: 4. Which country does the current Secretary-General of SAARC, Golam Sarwar, represent?
explain: Current Secretary-General Golam Sarwar represents Bangladesh. The other options are other member states.

q: 5. Which member state pays the largest voluntary contribution share (30.32%) to the SAARC budget?
explain: India contributes the largest share (30.32%) to the voluntary budget. Pakistan pays 22.52%; Bangladesh and Nepal pay 10.72%.

q: 6. What is the voluntary budget contribution share of Nepal in SAARC?
explain: Nepal pays a 10.72% share. 30.32% is India's, 22.52% is Pakistan's, and 5.00% is Bhutan's/Maldives'/Afghanistan's share.

q: 7. Which three countries contribute exactly 10.72% each to the SAARC budget?
explain: These three nations contribute exactly 10.72% each. The other options feature different percentage brackets.

q: 8. In which country was the historic First SAARC Summit held in December 1985?
explain: The 1st SAARC Summit was held in Dhaka, Bangladesh, on December 7-8, 1985. The other options hosted later summits.

q: 9. How many SAARC summits have been successfully hosted in Kathmandu, Nepal to date?
explain: Kathmandu, Nepal, has hosted four summits successfully (3rd, 11th, 18th, and 21st). Three excludes the 2023 21st Summit.

q: 10. Which SAARC summits were held in Kathmandu, Nepal?
explain: Kathmandu hosted these four summits in 1987, 2002, 2014, and 2023. The other options list summits hosted elsewhere.

q: 11. Which Nepalese delegate participated on behalf of Nepal in the First SAARC Summit in 1985?
explain: King Birendra represented Nepal at the 1st Summit in 1985. King Gyanendra represented Nepal in 2005; the others represented Nepal in later years as Prime Ministers.

q: 12. Who was the first Prime Minister of Nepal to represent the country in a SAARC Summit (5th Summit, 1990)?
explain: Prime Minister KP Bhattarai represented Nepal at the 5th Summit in Male (1990). The other options represented Nepal at later summits.

q: 13. Which Prime Minister represented Nepal at the 11th SAARC Summit held in Kathmandu in January 2002?
explain: PM Deuba represented Nepal at the 11th Summit in Kathmandu (2002). The other options are other Prime Ministers who attended different summits.

q: 14. Who represented Nepal as the Head of State during the 13th SAARC Summit in Dhaka in November 2005?
explain: King Gyanendra represented Nepal at the 13th Summit in Dhaka. King Birendra attended the first four summits; Koirala and Koirala were Heads of Government.

q: 15. Which Prime Minister represented Nepal at the 18th SAARC Summit in Kathmandu in November 2014?
explain: PM Sushil Koirala represented Nepal at the 18th Summit in Kathmandu in November 2014. The other options represented Nepal at other summits.

q: 16. Which scheduled SAARC Summit was cancelled following the Uri Attack and India's subsequent withdrawal?
explain: The 19th Summit, scheduled for Islamabad in 2016, was cancelled due to the Uri Attack and India's withdrawal. The other options were held successfully.

q: 17. Where was the 19th SAARC Summit scheduled to be held before its cancellation?
explain: The 19th Summit was scheduled to be held in Islamabad. The other options represent other locations.

q: 18. Which country has hosted SAARC summits exactly three times, similar to Nepal?
explain: These nations, along with Nepal, have hosted summits exactly three times (or four for Nepal now). The other options are incorrect groupings.

q: 19. Which SAARC Summit was held in Kathmandu, Nepal, in the year 2023?
explain: The 21st Summit was convened in Kathmandu, Nepal, in 2023. The 18th Summit was in 2014; the 19th and 20th were scheduled or postponed.

q: 20. Who represented Nepal at the 17th SAARC Summit in Addu City, Maldives (2011)?
explain: PM Dr. Baburam Bhattarai represented Nepal at the 17th Summit in Addu City, Maldives (2011). The other options are other Prime Ministers.

q: 21. Who represented Nepal at the 8th SAARC Summit in New Delhi (1995)?
explain: PM Manmohan Adhikari represented Nepal at the 8th Summit in New Delhi (1995). The other options represented Nepal at other summits.

q: 22. How many summits did King Birendra Bir Bikram Shah attend as Nepal's representative?
explain: King Birendra represented Nepal at the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Summits. The other options do not match his record.

q: 23. Who signed the SAPTA Charter on behalf of the Government of Nepal?
explain: Finance Minister Mahesh Acharya signed SAPTA on behalf of Nepal. Dr. Bhesh Bahadur Thapa signed SAFTA; the others are Secretaries-General.

q: 24. At which Summit was the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement reached and signed in January 2004?
explain: SAFTA was negotiated and signed on January 6, 2004, at the 12th Summit in Islamabad. The other options hosted different trade achievements.

q: 25. How many Articles are there in the charter of SAFTA?
explain: SAFTA, like SAPTA, contains exactly 25 Articles in its charter. The other options do not represent the correct article count.

q: 26. During which summit was the SAARC Agreement on Trade in Services (SATIS) signed in April 2010?
explain: SATIS was signed during the 16th Summit in Thimphu, Bhutan, in April 2010. The other options hosted different summit frameworks.

q: 27. When did the SAARC Agreement on Trade in Services (SATIS) officially enter into force?
explain: SATIS entered into force on November 29, 2012. April 2010 is the signing year; January 1, 2006 is SAFTA's active date.

q: 28. Where is the headquarters of the SAARC Development Fund (SDF) situated?
explain: The SAARC Development Fund is headquartered in Thimphu. The other options host other specialized bodies or centers.

q: 29. In which country is the South Asian University (SAU) located?
explain: The South Asian University (SAU) is an international university located in New Delhi, India. The other options are other member nations.

q: 30. Where is the Secretariat of the South Asian Regional Standards Organization (SARSO) located?
explain: SARSO (Standards Organization) has its permanent Secretariat in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The other options host other specialized institutions.

q: 31. Which intergovernmental body of SAARC is located in Islamabad, Pakistan to provide a forum for commercial and trade dispute resolution?
explain: The Arbitration Council is located in Islamabad, Pakistan, for legal dispute resolution. The other options are based in other member capitals.

q: 32. Before the 18th Summit, the SAARC regional centers were consolidated from eleven down to how many?
explain: Regional centers were consolidated from eleven down to five to reduce redundant expenses before the 18th Summit. The other options represent other administrative counts.

q: 33. Which is the oldest regional center of SAARC, established in 1989?
explain: SAC is the oldest center, established in 1989 in Dhaka. STAC was established in 1992, SEC in 2006, and SCC in 2009.

q: 34. Where is the SAARC TB and HIV/AIDS Centre (STAC) located?
explain: STAC is located in Bhaktapur, Nepal. Kathmandu and Pokhara are other Nepalese cities; Dhaka is in Bangladesh.

q: 35. In which year was the SAARC TB Centre established, which was later renamed STAC in November 2007?
explain: The SAARC TB Centre started functioning in 1994 and was renamed STAC in November 2007. 1989 is SAC's year, 1992 is STAC's regional center establishment year, and 2006 is SEC's establishment year.

q: 36. The SAARC Poverty Alleviation program was implemented in which district of Nepal?
explain: The SAARC Poverty Alleviation program was implemented in Nepal's Makwanpur district. The other options are other districts of Nepal not associated with this program.

q: 37. With which SAARC country does Nepal conduct the least amount of trade?
explain: Maldives is the SAARC country with which Nepal conducts the least trade. The other options have higher recorded trade volumes.

q: 38. What is the cash prize associated with the SAARC Award established in 2004?
explain: The SAARC Award cash prize is $25,000 (USD) along with a certificate. The other options are incorrect prize amounts.

q: 39. Who is the only person to be honored with the SAARC Award posthumously?
explain: Ziaur Rahman was posthumously honored as the only recipient of the SAARC Award. The other options are other historical figures of South Asia.

q: 40. When and under which treaty was SAARC officially established?
explain: SAARC was formally established on 8 December 1985 through the Dhaka Declaration, signed at the first SAARC Summit.

q: 41. Which of the following given dignitaries is/are not the signatories on the Charter of SAARC?
explain: Ziaur Rahman of Bangladesh, who first proposed the idea of regional cooperation, died in 1981, before the SAARC Charter was signed in 1985, so he could not be a signatory.

q: 42. Who was first raised the concept of regional, political and economical cooperation in South Asia?
explain: President Ziaur Rahman of Bangladesh is credited with first proposing the idea of regional cooperation in South Asia in the late 1970s.

q: 43. Which one of the following is not an objective of the SAARC charter?
options: To promote the welfare of the peoples of South Asia
To accelerate economic growth in South Asia
To contribute to mutual trust in South Asia
explain: "Maintaining international peace" is a UN Charter objective, not a stated objective of the SAARC Charter, which focuses on regional welfare, growth, and cooperation.

q: 44. For which of following, the SAARC movement was launched?
explain: SAARC was launched with the core aim of promoting regional cooperation among South Asian nations.

q: 45. Which of the following given is/are the principles of SAARC?
explain: Article II of the SAARC Charter lists sovereign equality, territorial integrity, and non-interference in internal affairs among its guiding principles.

q: 46. How many articles are there in Charter of SAARC?
explain: The SAARC Charter, signed in 1985, contains 10 Articles covering objectives, principles, institutional structure, and administration.

q: 47. How many Apex bodies are there in SAARC?
explain: SAARC has 6 recognized Apex bodies representing professional and civil society groups across the region.

q: 48. Which is the executive body of SAARC?
explain: The Standing Committee, composed of Foreign Secretaries, functions as the executive body overseeing programme implementation.

q: 49. In which Article of the SAARC Charter, the principles of the SAARC is mentioned?
explain: Article II of the SAARC Charter lays down the guiding principles of the organization.

q: 50. Which country is not the founder member of the SAARC?
explain: SAARC was founded in 1985 by seven countries; Afghanistan joined later, in 2007, becoming the eighth member.
